story: Broadening HSTS to secure more of the Web
text: Relevant part starts here [VIDEO] Although for anyone interested in HTTPS, I'd recommend watching the whole thing. Very entertaining.

This guide is very hand-wavey. Tor alone is a poor operational security strategy; using nikto and unix-privesc-check does not a hacker make. This may be a decent place to begin one's inquiry, but don't let it end here too. Here are some talks I recommend: Tricks for Defeating SSL in Practice - Moxie Marlinspike [VIDEO] OPSEC: Because Jail is for wuftpd - thegrugq [LINK]

story: Our First Certificate Is Now Live
text: We don't have humans in the loop for issuing certificate; this can and has been exploited for fun and profit, with fun attacks like getting a cert for "citibank.com\0.mydomain.com" which used to trick the C strcmp in most browser certificate checking routines. Moxie has an entertaining talk: [VIDEO] Your problem would be getting people to "thecitibank.com." Chrome, Firefox, and GMail would all eventually figure out it was a phishing site and warn users about clicking through to it.

Perhaps one of the techniques discussed here: [VIDEO] ? Or, as this was published a couple of days ago, it might have utilized POODLE, or even BEAST in unmitigated cases. But yeah, I'd also believe user error in some cases.

story: Alibaba’s UC Browser is dominating in Asian markets with lower-end smartphones
text: History lesson incoming: [VIDEO] The only effective way to get guaranteed security is with HSTS preloading. Anything short of that leaves you vulnerable to the linked attack, which dates way back to 2012.
